text: Rounded rectangles added in 87e8a12. Grob.rect(..., cornerRadius: ExtentExpr = ExtentExpr.zero) resolves the radius the way a circle radius resolves -- the smaller of the two axis resolutions, so a relative unit cannot distort a corner on an anisotropic frame -- and DeviceScene lowering clamps it to half the shorter resolved side. That is the SVG rx/ry rule applied once, so every backend rounds the same corner: SVG emits rx/ry, Java2D builds a RoundRectangle2D (doubling the radius into AWT's arc width, which AWT halves back), Canvas and JavaFX trace the four-corner arcTo path, PDF emits four Beziers using the same quarter-circle control ratio appendCircle already used. DevicePrimitive.RectShape gained cornerRadius between height and gp. Acceptance met: a zero radius renders byte-identically to before, pinned by SvgGrobFormSuite's exact <rect> string with no rx attribute; RendererConformance gains a rounded-rect case with one ordinary and one over-large radius, so every backend harness draws both and the bounding box is unchanged; RectCornerLaws (intaglio-laws) pins zero-radius identity, bounding-box invariance under any radius, the clamp limit, that an oversized request resolves to exactly half the shorter side, and that a negative or non-finite radius is unrepresentable -- ExtentExpr refuses one, so refusal is at construction as asked. Not established: no pinned raster golden or paired ggplot2 visual-QA case shows a rounded corner, so cross-backend corner rendering is proved by conformance and law rather than by image. Corner rounding is uniform (rx == ry); independent horizontal and vertical radii are not expressible.
